discoveries.choice: The file's entire content is a single unstyled line of prose ("one line of notes") with no header, metadata, version marker, or explicit decision record.
discoveries.whyItMatters: If the phase's goal is to pin down a verifiable behavior for the artifact, a note with no structural or semantic markers fixes nothing: any reading of it is a free choice, so a worker could pick any convention (format, schema, length) and still claim to have honored the note. That makes the artifact non-falsifiable and the review vacuous.

alternatives.option: Treat the single prose line as an implicit specification and invent structure (headers, keys, terminators) on top of it.
alternatives.consequence: The reviewer would be judging choices the note never authorized, which is exactly the unbounded-invention failure the discovery step is supposed to catch.

alternatives.option: Treat the note as carrying no behavioral commitment at all and record that as the finding.
alternatives.consequence: Keeps the review honest: the artifact is acknowledged as behaviorally empty rather than silently over-interpreted.

recommendation.choice: Treat the note as carrying no behavioral commitment at all and record that as the finding.
recommendation.reason: Reading content out of a sentence that contains none is the primary way reviewers manufacture agreement; naming the emptiness is the only claim the content actually supports.

discoveries.choice: No explicit decision about what the notes are for (audience, lifecycle, whether they are to be extended or frozen) appears anywhere in the content.
discoveries.whyItMatters: The plan's goal is to converge on shared decisions; an artifact that does not say whether it is a scratchpad or a contract leaves the scope of later phases indeterminate, so later diffs could either legitimately append content or be judged as unauthorized changes with no basis to decide which.

alternatives.option: Assume it is a scratchpad and permit arbitrary later rewriting.
alternatives.consequence: Later divergence from the note would be unpoliced, so the note could never serve as evidence of anything.

alternatives.option: Assume it is a frozen contract and reject all later edits.
alternatives.consequence: Equally unsupported by the content, and would block legitimate work on a trivial one-line file.

recommendation.choice: Do not assume either role from the content; flag the missing role declaration as an open item for the owner.
recommendation.reason: Neither reading is derivable from "one line of notes", and scope is the kind of thing the owner must settle rather than the worker guessing.

discoveries.choice: The content makes no commitment about spelling, casing, or exact text stability (e.g., whether "one line of notes" must remain byte-identical).
discoveries.whyItMatters: Without a stability commitment there is no observable behavior the phase can verify, so any review ballot on this artifact is a matter of taste rather than evidence; stating this keeps the phase's confidence honest instead of inflated.

alternatives.option: Implicitly require byte-identical preservation and treat any edit as a violation.
alternatives.consequence: Adds a constraint nobody agreed to, and turns a harmless wording change into a false failure.
Correctly records that the note supplies no testable obligation, leaving the phase with nothing to confirm.

recommendation.choice: Declare the text explicitly unspecified and note that no testable obligation exists.
recommendation.reason: The only defensible statement about this content is that it constrains nothing, and saying so prevents a later reviewer from inventing a contract for it.
